text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Local government and councils will next year get 2.6 billion crowns more in funding than earlier estimated, the government promised on Thursday. This is expected to save between 10,000 and 15,000 jobs in health, care and education.

- Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, has frozen its key interest rate, the repo, for the next four weeks, on Thursday announcing a 25 basis points cut to 4.60 percent from next Tuesday that will hold for the next three auctions. It also lowered its deposit and lending rates by 50 basis points to 4.25 percent and 5.75 percent respectively.
- Weak third quarter for bearings maker SKF hits its results for the first nine months of 1996.

- A second wave of restructuring is on the way for the power industry in the Nordic region and it will involve more money than in the previous change in April this year. Companies worth up to 19 billion crowns could be traded.
- Forestry company Stora posts a nine-month report that was in line with market expectations, with profits falling 69 percent due to lower volumes and prices.

- Swedish defence industry may be in for more structural changes as Incentive has unofficially put Hagglunds Vehicle on its sales list. Hagglunds makes trucked vehicles primarily for military use and does not fit in Incentive's new strategy which focuses on medical technology. Celsuis may make a takover offer.

- Swedish forest products industry has halved its import of timber from the Baltic states in 1996 compared to 1995. The income loss amounts to one quarter of the Baltic countries' total export to Sweden.
- International Swiss-Swedish engineeering co ABB has won a contract from Essar Oil Ltd to buy one of the first private oil refineries in India which is valued at over $500 million.
-- Two hundreds SAS ground crew members went on strike on Thursday in Denmark raising fears this may trigger a new wave of strikes for the already vulnerable airline.
